bands.1:
Bluster Rock is a big red rock in the sea. The wind never stops. It blows red dust into your ears.

"There is a 64 per cent chance of dust in your socks," says Tully.

Mo makes beetroot damper with jellybeans. It crunches.

"That's disgusting," says Tully. A red lizard puffs up like a balloon. It is a Puffentie. Strong words make it swell.

"Why did the boulder go to sales school?" asks Mo. "To be a little bolder!"

Everyone groans.

At the top of the rock is a huge gold warehouse. The sign says, "VANTAMART. EVERY DOLLAR GOES TO THE RESCUE FUND!"

A speaker shouts, "Smash that BUY button like it owes you money!" Then it sings, "Buy a hoodie, save a Creature!"

"He always sings that bit flat," says Wren, so quietly that only you hear.

"ROLL UP, ROLL UP!"

A man jumps out from under a red umbrella. He has a striped suit and a curly moustache. A kookaburra sits on the umbrella.

"I'm Slick Vinnie!" he cries. "Buy a Mozzie-Proof Hat! Everybody has one! Can you afford NOT to?"

Nearby, a Bilbolster's big ears flop down. The kookaburra laughs. "Koo-koo-ha-ha-HA!"

"That's Spruikoo," says Vinnie. "He laughs when you can't back something up."

"I'll buy two," says Gus.

"Don't," you say. "Nobody is wearing one. Not even him."

Vinnie grins. "A customer who doesn't buy! I like you."

You ask about the Vantamart. Vinnie stops smiling.

"That sign has no numbers and no proof," he says. "And no Creatures ever come out."

"Will you help us?" you ask.

"Win my badge first, Captain," says Vinnie. "Prove nobody can sell you anything. Would I lie to you?"

Spruikoo opens his beak. Then he shuts it.

That night, a back door opens at the Vantamart. Two Goldies push out a box.

Something inside it is scratching.

The label says, "LIVE MERCH. DO NOT FEED."

"There's a 64 per cent chance of red dust in your socks by lunchtime," says Tully.

Mo serves beetroot-and-jellybean damper. It crunches in all the wrong places.

"That's disgusting," says Tully. Nearby, a big red lizard puffs up to twice its size. It's a Puffentie. Emotive words make it swell like a balloon.

"Why did the boulder go to sales school?" asks Mo. "It wanted to be a little bolder!"

Everyone groans.

The island is full of Creatures. A Proovil suns itself with its spikes standing up. A Bilbolster pokes its head out of a burrow.

At the bottom of the rock is a noisy market. At the top is an enormous gold warehouse. A billboard on the roof flashes: "VANTAMART. EVERY DOLLAR GOES TO THE RESCUE FUND!"

A speaker blares Maxx's voice. "Smash that BUY button like it owes you money!" Then a jingle plays. "Buy a hoodie, save a Creature!"

"He always sings that bit flat," mutters Wren, so quietly that only you hear.

"ROLL UP, ROLL UP!"

A man in a striped suit leaps out from under a big red umbrella. His moustache is waxed into two perfect curls. A kookaburra sits on top of the umbrella.

"Slick Vinnie, at your service!" cries the man. "Behold the deal of the century: the Mozzie-Proof Hat! Ten thousand sold this morning! Everybody's wearing one! Can you really afford NOT to?"

The Bilbolster's ears flop flat. The kookaburra cackles. "Koo-koo-ha-ha-HA!"

"That's Spruikoo," sighs Vinnie. "He laughs whenever someone says something they can't back up. Terrible for business."

"I'll take two," says Gus.

"Don't," you say. "Nobody here is wearing one. Not even him."

Vinnie freezes. Then he grins. "A customer who doesn't buy! I haven't met one of those in twenty years."

You ask him about the Vantamart. For the first time, Vinnie stops selling.

"I know a sales pitch when I hear one, Captain," he says. "'Every dollar goes to the Rescue Fund'? No numbers. No receipts. And not one Creature walking out the front door."

"Will you help us get inside?" you ask.

"Win my badge, Captain," says Vinnie. "Prove nobody can sell you anything. Then we'll talk business. Would I lie to you?"

Spruikoo opens his beak, thinks about it, and closes it again.

That night, Zed watches the Vantamart through his binoculars. A back door slides open. Two Goldies wheel out a single crate.

Something inside it is scratching.

Zed zooms in on the label. "LIVE MERCH. DO NOT FEED."
bands.3:
Bluster Rock rises out of the sea like a giant red loaf of bread that has been left in the oven far too long. The wind never stops blowing. It whips red dust off the cliffs and pours it straight into your ears.

"Statistically," says Tully, spitting out grit, "there's a 64 per cent chance of red dust in your socks by lunchtime."

Mo serves beetroot-and-jellybean damper. It crunches in all the wrong places.

"That's disgusting," says Tully. On a rock nearby, a big red lizard puffs up to twice its size. It's a Puffentie, and emotive words make it swell like a balloon.

"Why did the boulder go to sales school?" asks Mo. "It wanted to be a little bolder!"

Everyone groans.

The island is crawling with Creatures. A Proovil, a thorny devil, suns itself with its spikes standing straight up. A Bilbolster pokes its head out of a burrow, ears swivelling like satellite dishes. A flock of Squawkles screeches from a dead tree.

At the bottom of the rock is a noisy market of tents and flapping flags. At the top, glittering against the cliffs, is an enormous gold warehouse. Trucks crawl in and out, loaded with gold hoodies and life-sized Maxx pillows. A billboard on the roof flashes: "VANTAMART. EVERY DOLLAR GOES TO THE RESCUE FUND!"

A speaker blares Maxx's voice. "Smash that BUY button like it owes you money!" Then comes the jingle. "Buy a hoodie, save a Creature! Maxx it out, it's a double feature!"

"He always sings that bit flat," mutters Wren, so quietly that only you hear.

"ROLL UP, ROLL UP!"

A man in a red-and-white striped suit leaps out from under a big red umbrella. His hair is slicked back so hard it shines, and his moustache is waxed into two perfect curls. On top of the umbrella sits a kookaburra with a very smug expression.

"Slick Vinnie, at your service!" cries the man. "Friends, behold the deal of the century: the Mozzie-Proof Hat! Ten thousand sold this morning! Everybody's wearing one! Can you really afford NOT to?"

The Bilbolster's ears flop flat. The kookaburra throws back its head and cackles. "Koo-koo-ha-ha-HA!"

"That's Spruikoo," sighs Vinnie. "He laughs whenever someone says something they can't back up. Terrible for business."

"I'll take two," says Gus.

"Don't," you say. "Nobody here is wearing one. Not even him."

Vinnie freezes. Then a slow grin spreads under his moustache. "A customer who doesn't buy," he says. "I haven't met one of those in twenty years."

You ask him about the Vantamart, and for the first time, Vinnie stops selling.

"I'll tell you something for free, Captain, which I never do," he says. "I've been spruiking at this market my whole life. I know a sales pitch when I hear one. 'Every dollar goes to the Rescue Fund'? No numbers. No receipts. And not one Creature walking out the front door."

"Koo-koo-ha-ha-HA!" laughs Spruikoo, at the billboard.

"Will you help us get inside?" you ask.

Vinnie twirls one curl of his moustache. "Win my badge, Captain. Prove nobody can sell you anything. Then we'll talk business. Would I lie to you?"

Spruikoo opens his beak, thinks about it, and politely closes it again.

That night, the crew lies on the deck, watching the Vantamart through Zed's binoculars. Then a back door slides open, and two Goldies in gold tracksuits wheel out a single crate.

Something inside it is scratching.

Zed zooms in on the label. It's stamped in gold capitals: "LIVE MERCH. DO NOT FEED."
bands.4:
Bluster Rock rises out of the sea like an enormous red loaf of bread that someone has left in the oven far too long. The wind here never stops blowing. It whips red dust off the cliffs, flings it across the water and pours it, as far as anyone can tell, directly into your ears.

"Statistically," says Tully, spitting out a mouthful of grit, "there's a 64 per cent chance of red dust in your socks by lunchtime, and a hundred per cent chance of it in your sandwiches."

"That's fine," says Mo. "Today's lunch is already red." He serves beetroot-and-jellybean damper, which crunches in all the wrong places.

"That's disgusting," says Tully. On a rock nearby, a big red perentie lizard puffs itself up to twice its size. It's a Puffentie, and emotive words make it swell like a beach ball.

"Why did the boulder go to sales school?" asks Mo, undeterred. "It wanted to be a little bolder!"

The groan is so loud and so long that the Puffentie puffs up all over again.

The island is crawling with Creatures. A Proovil, a thorny devil, basks on a warm rock with its spikes standing straight up. A Bilbolster pokes its head out of a burrow, ears swivelling like satellite dishes. A flock of pink-and-grey Squawkles screeches from a dead tree, each of them determined to be the loudest bird in history.

At the bottom of the rock sprawls a noisy market of tents, trestle tables and flapping flags. At the top, glittering against the red cliffs, squats an enormous gold warehouse. Trucks crawl in and out of it all day, loaded with gold hoodies, Maxx lunchboxes and life-sized Maxx pillows. A billboard on the roof flashes: "VANTAMART. EVERY DOLLAR GOES TO THE RESCUE FUND!"

Below the billboard, a speaker blares Maxx's voice on a loop. "Smash that BUY button like it owes you money! Two Xs, because one X is for losers!" Then comes the jingle. "Buy a hoodie, save a Creature! Maxx it out, it's a double feature!"

"That doesn't even rhyme properly," says Indi.

"He always sings that bit flat," mutters Wren, so quietly that only you hear.

"ROLL UP, ROLL UP!"

A man in a red-and-white striped suit springs out from under a big red umbrella. His hair is slicked back so hard that it shines, and his moustache is waxed into two perfect curls. On top of the umbrella perches a kookaburra with an enormous beak and an extremely smug expression.

"Slick Vinnie, at your service!" cries the man. "Friends, you look like people who deserve the deal of the century! Behold the Mozzie-Proof Hat! Ten thousand sold this morning alone! Everybody's wearing one! Can you really afford NOT to?"

The Bilbolster's ears flop flat. The kookaburra throws back its head and cackles. "Koo-koo-ha-ha-HA!"

"That's Spruikoo," sighs Vinnie. "He laughs whenever somebody says something they can't back up. Terrible for business."

"I'll take two," says Gus, already reaching for his pocket.

"Don't," you say. "Nobody here is wearing one. Not even him."

Vinnie freezes. Then a slow grin spreads beneath his moustache. "Well, well, well," he says. "A customer who doesn't buy. I haven't met one of those in twenty years."

You ask him about the Vantamart. Vinnie glances up at the golden warehouse, and for the first time since you arrived, he stops selling.

"I'll tell you something for free, Captain, which is not something I usually do," he says. "I've been spruiking at this market since I was knee-high to a bilby. I know a sales pitch when I hear one. 'Every dollar goes to the Rescue Fund'? That's the biggest pitch I've ever heard. No numbers. No receipts. And not a single Creature walking out the front door."

"Koo-koo-ha-ha-HA!" laughs Spruikoo, at the billboard.

"So will you help us get inside?" you ask.

Vinnie twirls one curl of his moustache. "Win my badge, Captain. Prove that nobody can sell you anything. Then we'll talk business. Would I lie to you?"

Spruikoo opens his beak, considers the question carefully, and politely closes it again.

That night, the crew lies on the deck, watching the Vantamart through Zed's binoculars. The trucks have stopped, and the market below is dark and silent. Then a back door slides open, and two Goldies in gold tracksuits wheel out a single wooden crate.

Something inside it is scratching.

Zed zooms in on the label, stamped in gold capitals: "LIVE MERCH. DO NOT FEED."
